title: You didn’t notice it at first.
paragraphs: You didn’t notice it at first.
The voice sounded right. The words felt spiritual. The confidence was convincing. They spoke in the name of God, and nobody questioned it—especially not you.
Because they used Scripture.
Because they said “The Lord told me.”
Because they stood where truth is supposed to stand.
But something was off… and you felt it.
You ignored it.

God saw it.
You knew.
This isn’t new.
What you’re seeing today already happened in ancient Israel, and it didn’t end quietly—it ended in judgment.
Open Jeremiah and listen carefully:

“Thus says the Lord of hosts: ‘Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you. They make you worthless; they speak a vision of their own heart, not from the mouth of the Lord.’” (Jeremiah 23:16)
Read that again.
They spoke… but God did not send them.
They sounded spiritual… but they were inventing messages.
They stood in authority… but they were leading people away from truth.
And here’s what most people don’t realize…

False prophets don’t usually look dangerous.
They look anointed.

They don’t start with lies.
They start with almost-truth.
And almost-truth is enough to destroy you slowly.
In Israel, the people wanted comfort, not correction. They wanted peace, not repentance. So when false prophets said, “You’re fine… God is pleased… no judgment is coming,” the people leaned in.
It felt good.
It sounded merciful.
It was deadly.
“They have healed the wound of My people lightly, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace.” (Jeremiah 6:14)
Do you see it?
Spiritual authority was being used… to silence conviction.

Instead of exposing sin, they covered it.
Instead of calling repentance, they affirmed rebellion.
And the people followed them willingly.
That’s the part that should unsettle you.

Because false prophets don’t rise in isolation.
They rise because people prefer them.

You preferred the message that didn’t confront you.
You leaned toward the voice that didn’t demand change.
You stayed where your sin wasn’t threatened.

God saw it.
You knew.
In Ezekiel, God speaks even more sharply:
“Woe to the foolish prophets, who follow their own spirit and have seen nothing!” (Ezekiel 13:3)
Nothing.
No vision from God. No word from heaven. Just imagination… dressed up as revelation.
And yet they still spoke with authority.
That’s the danger.
Authority without truth is not harmless—it is destructive.
Because people don’t just listen… they trust.
And when spiritual leaders abuse that trust, they don’t just mislead—they distort people’s view of God Himself.
That’s why God’s response is severe:
“I am against the prophets,” declares the Lord, “who steal My words from one another.” (Jeremiah 23:30)
Against them.
Not mildly correcting. Not overlooking.
Against.
Let that settle.
Because some of the voices you admire… God may be opposing.
And if you’re following them, you’re walking in that opposition too.
Now here’s where it gets uncomfortable.
This isn’t just about “them.”
It’s about what you tolerate.
It’s about what you share, what you repost, what you sit under without testing.
Because Scripture already warned you:
“Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits, whether they are of God…” (1 John 4:1)

You weren’t called to consume blindly.
You were called to discern.
But discernment requires something most people avoid:
Truth that cuts.
Truth that exposes.
Truth that leads you to repentance.
And this is where everything shifts.
Because the solution to false prophets is not better prophets.
It’s the true Gospel.
Not comfort.
Not motivational spirituality.
Not vague “God loves you” messages detached from sin.
The real Gospel begins where false prophecy refuses to go:
Your sin.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)

Not some people.
Not just the obvious sinners.
You.
And false prophets will never stay there long… because if they did, they would have to take you to repentance.
And repentance costs you something.
But grace meets you there.
“But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
That’s the difference.
False prophets say: “You’re fine.”
Jesus says: “You’re not… but I came to save you.”
False prophets protect your comfort.
Jesus confronts your sin… then gives you life.
And the cross is where every false voice is exposed.
Because no one who truly stands under the authority of Jesus Christ can ignore sin, skip repentance, and still speak for God.
It’s impossible.
So now you’re at a line.
Not emotionally.
Spiritually.
You can keep following voices that feel good but lead nowhere…
Or you can return to the truth that wounds before it heals.
One path numbs you.
The other saves you.
If something in you is tightening right now… that’s not condemnation.
That’s exposure.
And it’s mercy.
Say it plainly if you feel it: “Lord, I don’t want deception anymore.”
Not for show.
Not for others.
For you.
Because this doesn’t end with information.
It ends with a decision.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.

Follow if you’re done playing with half-truths and ready for the real Gospel.
Because the most dangerous deception… is the one that still sounds like God.
